A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: v1 reports original VQA experiments, retrieval-efficiency measurements, boundary-identification results, and appendix evaluations on DeepSeek and MMMU.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a comparison of Qwen-Max and GPT-4o as evaluators on Mix.

M1.justification: The response-sampling and scoring pipeline, hard and soft training objectives, training prompts, and retrieval decision procedure remain unchanged in Section 2 and Appendix A.1.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluation coverage remain unchanged, including Life VQA, Private VQA, Chinese/English Dyn-VQA, NoCaps, Visual7W, Mix, and appendix MMMU. The new evaluator comparison uses the existing Mix dataset.

E2.justification: No RAG, All RAG, Prompt-based, and Human retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons, with the same VLLMs. GPT-4o's additional evaluator role in v2 Table 8 does not change the methods compared against HKB and SKB.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.5 introduces GPT-4o scoring alongside Qwen-Max for four VLLMs under No RAG and All RAG on Mix. The original experimental settings are retained; the newly disclosed gradient-accumulation value does not establish a training-protocol change.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 and Table 8 add an evaluator-consistency analysis, examining how aggregate Mix scores differ between Qwen-Max and GPT-4o judges. Existing threshold-sensitivity, surrogate-boundary, held-in accuracy, and MMMU subject analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Response sampling remains R=30, and Table 1 retains the same mean and standard-deviation reporting. No seed, repeated-run, confidence-interval, significance-test, or uncertainty-estimation changes are introduced. The new evaluator table reports aggregate scores.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and plotted results are unchanged after matching relocated tables and figures. New Table 8 adds GPT-4o-judged Mix scores: for Qwen-VL-Chat, No RAG/All RAG score 32.62/38.34, alongside the retained Qwen-Max scores of 34.44/38.60. These are additional evaluator-dependent results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(8), including the training objectives and retrieval gate, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: learning hard and soft knowledge boundaries reduces retrieval while maintaining or improving VQA performance, and identified boundaries can serve as surrogates for other VLLMs.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 expands the explanation for overlapping knowledge boundaries, citing shared pretraining corpora, similar CLIP-based visual encoders, and common web-text knowledge. v1 offered a largely intuitive overlap argument. The stated limitations and interpretation of MMMU results remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Table 7 newly specifies 16 gradient-accumulation steps. Appendix A.4 adds approximately 10 hours of training on one A100 and API-call counts for data construction, retrieval, inference, and scoring. Table 6 clarifies the software name as ms-swift. These additions document existing implementation and resource requirements.

R1.justification: v2 adds Brown et al. (2020), Language Models are Few-Shot Learners, and Schuhmann et al. (2022), LAION-5B. The latter supports the expanded shared-pretraining rationale. The related-work sections and overall novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits refine grammar, change Visual to Vision in the VLLM introduction, standardize GPT-4o naming, and remove one author-email line. Two appendix subsections are inserted and subsequent references updated; most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds evaluator-comparison Table 8 and a gradient-accumulation row in Table 7. Figures 3 and 4 and several tables are relocated, with subsequent appendix tables renumbered. Existing figure artwork and plotted data remain unchanged within the same two-column layout.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility through the added implementation and training/API-cost disclosures, and provides useful evidence about evaluator dependence. The validation gain is limited: Table 8 covers aggregate No RAG/All RAG scores on Mix, and the judges reverse their ordering for GPT-4o outputs. These additions improve transparency without establishing stronger selective-retrieval performance or materially changing the method.
